newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai PM says plans to talk to Burma generals.
newsitem.headline: New Thai PM says plans to talk to Burma generals.

text.p: Thailand's newly-appointed prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Tuesday he planned to talk to Burma's ruling generals to explain how the world felt about Rangoon's human rights situation.

Chavalit, a general and former Thai army chief, said he wanted to tell leaders of Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) that the world had changed and it was time to change along with it.

"I want to say 'Please listen to me, something is going to change, you can't stay on like this anymore. Many people are talking about human rights, democracy...and you still do like this'," Chavalit told foreign reporters in his first briefing since his official appointment as Thailand's 22nd prime minister.
"I will go talk to them. Let them understand what's going on in the region, about globalisation," he said. "I don't want to leave them alone. We have to do our best to try and help them."
Chavalit has close ties to Burma's generals dating back to his time as Thai army chief.

The SLORC, which took power in 1988 following bloody pro-democracy demonstrations that left thousands dead or in jail, has faced international accusations of violating human rights and of suppressing the democracy movement.

Countries like the United States and European Union nations have recently slapped visa bans on senior SLORC officials because of Rangoon's renewed crackdown on the democracy movement headed by Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.
Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party won a landslide victory in a 1990 general election, a result not recognised by the SLORC.
